units.title: Prejudice and Discrimination
units.intro: Grammar: subject–verb agreement in complex sentences, and the present perfect and past perfect passive.

cards.title: Agreement in complex sentences
rule: Find the **real subject** even when other words come between it and the verb: *The **rights** of every citizen **are** protected.* *The **list** of complaints **is** long.*
A relative clause verb agrees with its antecedent: *people who **are** ...; a person who **is** ...*. A title or name of one thing is singular: *“Things Fall Apart” **is** a famous novel.*

One of the girls is absent.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Aster ________ in this biotechnology laboratory since she graduated from university five years ago.

steps.text: The time-marker 'since she graduated' indicates an action that started in the past and continues to the present, requiring the Present Perfect Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{has/have been} + \text{V-ing}$$).
Students often see 'is working' (Option A) and choose it because they think of it as an ongoing present action.
However, 'since' requires the perfect aspect, making 'has been working' (Option C) correct.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The construction company ________ the new highway road project three weeks ago.

steps.text: The definite past time-marker 'three weeks ago' requires the Simple Past tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_2$$).
Students often confuse Present Perfect 'has completed' (Option A) with Simple Past 'completed' (Option B).
Present Perfect cannot be used with definite past time-markers like 'three weeks ago'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Look at those thick dark clouds hanging over the mountains! It ________ rain very soon.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The public train to Djibouti ________ from the main station at exactly 7:30 AM tomorrow.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**

lessons.title: Present perfect and past perfect passive

cards.title: Present perfect and past perfect passive
rule: **has/have been + pp:** *New laws **have been passed** to stop discrimination.* **had been + pp:** *Before 1991 many people **had been denied** their rights.*

examples.text: Women have been given equal rights.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **Cross out** the words between the subject and verb, then check agreement.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Find the real subject before choosing the verb: one of, the number of and titles are singular; a number of is plural. Present perfect passive = has/have been + pp; past perfect passive = had been + pp.
